source.title: A Physics-Inspired Optimizer: Velocity Regularized Adam
source.authors: Pranav Vaidhyanathan; Lucas Schorling; Natalia Ares; Michael A. Osborne

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training loss and accuracy for ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10 with Adam, VRAdam, and SAM, bearing on whether training reaches low error. This is a different optimizer comparison from the claim versions’ stated tests.
record.gate_note: The paper says training stopped when loss fell below 0.1 or accuracy reached 0.97, and describes the training curves as showing faster convergence for VRAdam. Curve values are figure-only; no exact training-error result is stated. The CIFAR-10 benchmark table reports validation and test loss, not training classification error, so it is not included as a row.
record.test_reason: The Adam comparator reports training accuracy for ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10, bearing on V1. However, early stopping and unavailable plotted values prevent determining whether training classification error approaches zero. The adaptive-optimizer stability analysis does not test V5's specified dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Section 4.1: the authors report faster training convergence for VRAdam than Adam and SAM, without stating exact final training classification error. Their broader conclusion also claims improved benchmark performance and hyperparameter robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Studies a velocity-regularized Adam optimizer and its comparisons on ResNet-32 CIFAR-10; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ specified experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: VRAdam reportedly reduces training loss and increases training accuracy faster than Adam and SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Velocity-dependent global learning-rate damping can accelerate optimization relative to the tested optimizer baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: The study analyzes preconditioned sharpness and a changing effective learning rate for adaptive optimizers using batches of 1000, and supplies conditional stability arguments for momentum ablations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Velocity-dependent learning-rate damping modifies adaptive edge-of-stability dynamics.

record.problems: The training-curve findings are presented as figures without numeric values in the supplied text; the experiment uses one stated architecture and dataset, and the initialization is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The CIFAR-10 benchmark table reports validation and test loss for several optimizers, not training classification error, so it does not meet the row criteria for these versions.

untested.parts: Random initialization; CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; model-size effects; and systematic comparisons of early stopping or regularized recipes. Unrestricted convergence to near-zero classification error is not established by this stopped experiment.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, training speed attributable to initialization, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, divergence across learning-rate regimes, and full-batch sharpness approaching and remaining near the stability threshold.
Batch-normalization ablations, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is justified from the supplied text: Adam's final training accuracy cannot be read, and the stopping criteria cannot substitute for an observed endpoint. The omitted appendix training-loss plots do not supply training classification-error values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model-size effects, early stopping or regularized recipes as such, or compare SGD and Adam across model sizes.
